hold_text: This diff edits .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml and scripts/ci/check_automerge_trigger.py — TWO of the 11 entries in check_pr_landing.py::LANDING_MACHINERY — so R12 refuses it from self-landing and a human merges. That is correct and is not being routed around; a change to the landing route is exactly what wants one human read. ⚠️ THIS PR CANNOT TEST ITSELF, AND THAT IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT THING FOR THE READER TO KNOW: a workflow only runs from the version on `main`, so the changed job will not execute until after this merges. The decision half is therefore a PURE PYTHON MODULE with its own planted-defect suite, and the JS half was EXERCISED against a stub across five paths rather than only lint-checked — but neither is a live run. WHAT A HUMAN IS BEING ASKED TO READ: (1) the PR is created through a PAT-authenticated client when BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN is present, falling back LOUDLY to GITHUB_TOKEN when it is not; (2) auto-merge is armed only after scripts/ci/automerge_arming.py says a check has attached to the head. Both are strictly subtractive — (1) changes WHO opens the PR, (2) only ever WITHHOLDS arming — so neither can merge anything the current workflow would not have merged. ⚠️ THE ONE THING NOT ESTABLISHED: whether BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN carries PR-CREATE scope. It is used at 52 call sites for contents and branch-protection writes and that scope was NOT verified; it cannot be verified from a session, because the workflow only runs once merged. If the scope is missing, (1) falls back and (2) refuses, which is the SAFE direction but means PRs opened by this relay stop self-landing until the scope is granted. That trade is the merge decision, and it belongs to a human.
why: MI-280 unit U2, the PREVENTION half (the DETECTOR half is #11873, separate and already observed firing live). Tier-1 tooling throughout: .github/workflows/**, scripts/ci/**, tests/** — no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path, no strategy config, no risk cap. THE TIER IS NOT THE OBJECTION; the PATH is, and R12 is not to be defeated. THE MEASURED DEFECT, two facts that only bite together: GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN (recursion prevention), and this workflow opened the PR with exactly that token, so the pull_request event never fired and the required checks were never created — isolated in pr-opener.yml's own header on #10079 and re-measured on #10683, where a head pushed with the caller's own credentials STILL returned total_count 0. Arming is not a request to merge, it IS the merge, so arming such a PR hands the outcome to a head nothing is measuring. SIX instances on 2026-09-08 alone (#11356, #11392, #11395, #11407, #11419, #11424), and the 2026-09-12 one dropped the commit carrying a LIVE lane's registry row, leaving that lane running unrecorded on main for nine minutes. ⚠️ THE SUBTLETY THAT MAKES A NAIVE GATE VACUOUS AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THE DECISION IS A MODULE: a zero-check PR does NOT report zero check runs. It reports ONE — this job's own open-and-automerge, green because it succeeded at opening the PR. So check_runs.length > 0 is TRUE on precisely the PR the gate must refuse, and a gate written that way would pass every single time while reading like a real test. The self job is excluded BY NAME and a planted defect that stops excluding it fails the suite. THREE STATES, NEVER COLLAPSED: attached / none_attached / unreadable — the last is 'we could not look' and REFUSES, because an unread head is the head the gate exists to protect, not a safe one. There is deliberately NO override flag: the cheapest way past this gate must be to make the checks attach, and a test asserts no --force, FORCE_ARM, skip_gate or ARM_ANYWAY exists in the file. RECURRENCE: check_automerge_trigger.py gains C6 (the PR is created through a PAT-authenticated client) and C7 (the gate is invoked, PRECEDES the enable call, and its verdict is honoured), so a later editor cannot quietly delete the prevention; its self-test goes from 6 planted defects to 10. ⚠️ C6/C7 are SOURCE assertions and that limit is stated in the guard's own docstring rather than hidden: they establish that the workflow still ROUTES through the PAT and the gate, never that the gate DECIDES correctly — that half is the module's suite, which is why the decision lives there. VERIFICATION: 8 planted defects in automerge_arming.py, 8 caught by at least one probe, positive control quiet on restore. ⚠️ ONE PLANT ANCHOR WAS STALE on its first run and the harness printed STALE ANCHOR rather than silently not planting; it was re-run against the real text and the miss is recorded rather than counted, because a plant that does not plant is neither an escape nor a catch. 32 pytest cases including 4 mutation cases; 10/10 planted defects fail check_automerge_trigger.py with the clean tree passing as the positive control. THE JS WAS EXERCISED, NOT ONLY LINTED — five paths against a stub: no PAT (opens, warns, REFUSES) · PAT + real checks (opens as the PAT, ARMS) · the check read THROWS (unreadable, refuses) · an empty list (refuses) · THE GATE SCRIPT ITSELF UNRUNNABLE (setFailed, does NOT arm — the one thing a broken gate must never do is degrade to the behaviour it was added to prevent). AND THE GATE'S OWN SELF-TEST CAUGHT A BUG IN IT BEFORE IT SHIPPED: two nameless check entries are each != SELF_JOB, so a truthiness test on the remainder graded a PR with two empty stubs as fully attached — the arming-anyway outcome, reached by the tidiest line in the file. Fixed, with the reasoning written at the line.
